title: "How CI works"
description: "Public validation, review and delivery evidence for contributors."
audience: developers

GitHub Actions selects relevant checks from the repository workflows. Detailed operator runbooks are maintained privately.

## Validation and Delivery Evidence

Validate the exact source being proposed with the relevant focused checks. Record the commands and their outcomes, and distinguish local checks, CI, deployment identity and production behavior. A successful source check alone is not evidence of a deployment. Keep independent review and applicable release gates.

Deliver each verified change as soon as its required checks pass, and treat release schedules as latest-by times. After a deployment, a regression is fixed forward in the next deploy; roll back only when a fix cannot ship quickly or an active exploit or secret leak is involved. Independent apps and services deploy in parallel; serialize only for a proven dependency, such as a migration before the code that needs it, and record which dependency forced it.

Production migration prerequisites verify deployment-marker provenance separately
from marker status. The verifier binds the exact planner run and attempt to its
successful nested platform deployment job, marker-recording step and reviewed
producer contracts. Reusable workflows share their caller's run identity; they
do not supply a separate producer run. Staging source proof retains exact-source
and tree-equal direct-parent checks. These checks do not grant migration approval
or widen the existing manual recovery policy. A denied proof emits a fixed guard
code and phase in its result receipt; unavailable or changed evidence blocks apply.

Public build and merged-main test dispatches qualify the immutable dispatch
revision. The requested `source_sha` must equal that revision; a new dispatch
cannot select an older merged commit under newer workflow controls. Requalify a
historical source by rerunning its original workflow run. Fresh operator,
repository, run and current-policy checks still apply, so a policy change can
deny a historical rerun. Source jobs use hosted runners and read-only permissions;
this does not establish complete runtime-token isolation.

## Release bot sign-off for definer records

Ask for sign-off when an integration commit adds or rebinds records in
`scripts/ci/security-definer-verified-findings.json`. Review the exact commit's
ledger and migration changes. Use a single-commit integration push for this
workflow so the target's first parent is the base used by **Security Checks**.
GitHub must already be able to resolve the target commit. If it exists only
locally, dispatch after the authorized push and rerun the **Definer execution
policy** job on the original push run after sign-off.

From a checkout containing the integration commit, compute the required
description with the admission helper. Set `head` to the full integration SHA.

```bash
ledger=scripts/ci/security-definer-verified-findings.json
description=$(node scripts/ci/security-definer-admission.js digest \
  <(git show "${head}^1:$ledger") <(git show "$head:$ledger") | jq -er '.description')
gh workflow run release-bot-signoff.yaml --repo tutur3u/platform --ref main \
  -f sha="$head" -f context=security/definer-record-admission \
  -f description="$description"
```

Open the **Release bot sign-off** run in GitHub Actions. `vhpx` checks the
displayed SHA against the reviewed integration commit, selects **Review
deployments**, checks **release-bot-signoff**, and selects **Approve and deploy**.
The job recomputes the description from the two commit trees using the trusted
admission helper. The status links back to the approved workflow run.
Wait for the workflow to succeed before rerunning the original definer check.
The guard authenticates the workflow path and main dispatch, checks GitHub's
record of `vhpx` approving the protected environment, and verifies the immutable
run artifact that binds the status ID and ledger digest to the exact commit.
A copied run URL alone cannot satisfy admission.

If the integration SHA changes, recompute the description and dispatch again.
For a failed submission or expired receipt, check the status and workflow run
before starting a fresh dispatch and approval. Sign-off is limited to the
first attempt of each dispatch so that its approval history is unambiguous.

In repository settings, restrict the `release-bot-signoff` environment to the
`main` branch with `vhpx` as required reviewer and administrator bypass disabled.
The sign-off job uses its short-lived GitHub Actions token with read access
to contents and write access to commit statuses. No environment secret is
required. If the environment is recreated, update the pinned environment ID
in the admission verifier through the security review process.

## Label-gated heavy PR CI (`ready-for-ci`)

Heavy PR workflows require the `ready-for-ci` label. Non-draft pull requests from the same repository are eligible on `opened` and `ready_for_review`; forks are excluded from automatic admission. Independent review and green exact-head CI remain separate merge requirements. Run focused pre-push checks on an admitted development machine to reduce avoidable first-run failures. Skipped checks are not executed verification.

`auto-ready-for-ci.yaml` labels eligible pull requests using live pull-request metadata. It runs hosted metadata-only code from the base branch, without checking out or executing PR code. It is always-on admission automation rather than an affected-path validation job. Configure `CI_ADMISSION_TOKEN` as a token scoped only to this repository, with issues write and pull requests read permissions. A GitHub App installation token requires an existing rotation supplier; a fine-grained token requires expiry and renewal ownership. No token is created or installed by the workflow. Do not reuse the release administrator token.

The separate token is required because labels written with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger the `labeled` CI event. A missing admission token fails visibly; there is no fallback that adds a label without starting CI. Already-labelled PRs are unchanged. Before activation, the token supplier and independent workflow review must be accepted. An operator may add the label through the existing authenticated GitHub route while that supplier is unavailable.

Public pull-request jobs use GitHub-hosted runners. Self-hosted CI is restricted to trusted `push` or `workflow_dispatch` jobs on `main`; it must not execute fork PR code or receive production secrets. Machine admission and production-host headroom remain mandatory.

## Authorized CI Queue Cleanup

Cancellation needs explicit authorization for its scope. Identify each run and its source before acting, preserve required release and deployment work, and record the observed outcome. A branch name alone does not establish that a run is redundant.

## Draft PR runner admission

Draft status defers heavy verification where configured. Security eligibility and required checks follow the checked-in workflows. Moving a PR out of draft does not itself establish review approval or successful verification.

## Hosted runner reservation and PR queue pressure

Batch reviewable changes and use authorized local or development-runner checks to reduce PR queue pressure. Queue position and concurrency settings do not guarantee release capacity. Preserve the source identity and evidence for every reported result.

## Meet, Lettin, and Parley Cloudflare validation

App validation covers the affected application and its dependencies. Verify build metadata against the candidate source where required. Local tests, emitted artifacts and deployed behavior are distinct evidence; passing one does not establish the others.

## PR runner pool: variable, canary and kill switch

PR verification can use a separately admitted runner pool. Routing follows trusted workflow policy and must preserve isolation for untrusted contributions. Pool routing does not replace the PR label gate or independent review. Operator configuration and recovery procedures are maintained privately.

## Report-only Web E2E

The report-only Web browser workflow runs smoke or broader browser verification according to its trigger. It supplies browser evidence; it does not deploy the application. Its workflow-specific runtime exception does not resume other paused runtimes.

The job runs on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu and installs Chromium with its Linux system dependencies. The scoped launcher admits only the trusted main workflow on GitHub-hosted Linux. The launcher carries only allowlisted nonsecret admission fields through the synthetic BuildKit `web_env`. The build entrypoint rechecks those fields before selecting Turbo Web `build:docker` with dependency builds at concurrency 1; missing context retains the paused root alias and invalid context is rejected. Keep fleet verification static; Docker and browser execution belong to the hosted job.

Inspect the Smoke or Nightly step and its reports for browser acceptance. A successful report-only workflow can contain a failed job, and a provisioning failure does not prove that browser tests ran. The dependency image must copy every workspace manifest and file-backed dependency before its frozen install; the focused CI dependency-context test checks that inventory.

The admitted job restores E2E-owned Bun and Chromium download caches using exact
lockfile, platform and dependency inputs without fallback keys. Bun also includes
its pinned version, workspace manifests and patches. Frozen dependency install
and Chromium's Linux system-dependency install run on both hits and misses.
Only non-Dependabot main pushes save these archives, after successful installs;
the uncompressed limits are 512 MiB for Bun and 1 GiB for Chromium. Missing,
oversized or malformed size measurements skip the save. Scheduled and manual
runs restore matching archives without creating new generations.

These caches contain downloaded dependencies, not built applications, credentials,
browser auth state or database volumes. Runtime setup, disposable identities,
database reset and health checks remain required. Inspect restore hit outputs and
the individual install-step durations when comparing cold and warm runs. A cache
hit does not establish browser acceptance or a measured performance improvement.

## Repository cache budget

CI caches reduce repeated downloads and setup work. Cache availability is not guaranteed, and eviction can require fresh downloads. Reusing a cache never substitutes for checking the candidate source and dependency identity.

Fixed Supabase seed-catalog callers can opt into `pin-cache-key` to bind image
pins as well as the service list and platform; default producer/consumer keys
remain compatible. Fixed-catalog restores verify the source-pinned image config
digest and Linux/amd64 platform before use. That config digest identifies runtime
settings and filesystem-layer content under the
[OCI image configuration model](https://specs.opencontainers.org/image-spec/config/).
Registry pulls additionally require the pinned registry manifest reference.
[Docker save/load does not guarantee preserved registry references](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/43570),
so archive verification uses the content identity instead of relying on tag
presence or restored `RepoDigests`. Ordinary non-catalog consumers retain their
existing cache behavior. Hosted restore acceptance is separate from static tests.

## Frozen workflow installs

Workflow dependency installs use `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, and the retry helper adds the flag to project installs. Deliberate lockfile regeneration and pinned global CLI installs must match an exact workflow file, step name and full command in `scripts/ci/frozen-bun-install-exceptions.json`, and every exception disables lifecycle scripts. Run `node --test scripts/ci/frozen-bun-install-guard.test.js` to check the policy. Release credentials are scoped to the steps that push; operator details are maintained privately.

## CI summary

The `CI summary` check is one check run on the pull request head. `.github/workflows/ci-summary-poster.yml` computes it from the default branch. The workflow token is `contents: read`. It is not a `workflow_run` consumer. The dedicated CI admission App installation token posts the check. The job checks out the default branch only and does not run pull request code.

The check stays in progress while the pull request is a draft, an expected workflow has not started, or a run or check is still open. A completed workflow fails the summary when its conclusion is not success, including skipped and neutral. A completed check fails the summary unless its conclusion is success, skipped, or neutral. The summary succeeds only when every expected run is success and no other completed run or check on that head is failing. Expected workflows are the active default-branch workflows whose `pull_request` trigger matches the base branch, labels, and changed paths. An unreadable trigger stays expected. The summary's own check and workflow run are ignored. Path matching can over-match, which waits for more workflows instead of going green early.

`pull_request_target` posts the current picture. A schedule at minutes 7, 22, 37, and 52 refreshes every open pull request. GitHub may delay or drop a scheduled run, so a settled result can lag.

When `vars.CI_ADMISSION_APP_ID` and `secrets.CI_ADMISSION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are both absent, the poster job skips and logs "App not configured". It posts nothing and does not borrow another app's credentials. A partial or malformed configuration still fails closed, and the poster script refuses an installation token that lacks Checks write permission:

- `vars.CI_ADMISSION_APP_ID`: the dedicated CI admission App's numeric id.
- `secrets.CI_ADMISSION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`: that app's PEM private key.

Create the app for this repository, not as a grant of `checks: write` on the shared Actions token. Install it on `tutur3u/platform` with Actions read, Checks read and write, Contents read, Metadata read, and Pull requests read. Store `CI_ADMISSION_APP_ID` as a repository variable and `CI_ADMISSION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` as an Actions secret. The deleted workflow id `407998590` stays deleted; this poster is a different file.

### Test and Type Check draft admission

Test and Type Check defer every validation job while a pull request is a draft,
even if `ready-for-ci` remains present. `ready_for_review` admits validation once
the readiness label is present; `converted_to_draft` cancels superseded PR work
and starts a skipped run. Protected branch pushes retain validation. Check names
and aggregate failure assertions remain stable. Regression coverage:
`scripts/ci/test-type-draft-admission.test.js`.

The trusted App admission path must keep `opened` and `ready_for_review`: its App
label write generates the real `pull_request:labeled` event. Security classification
continues on drafts and bot-authored PRs. Summary metadata events retain draft and
label transitions so the displayed readiness state stays accurate.

### Opt-in Test and Type Check runners

`CI_VALIDATION_RUNNER` selects only the secret-free PR unit shards and PR Type
Check job. Empty, malformed or unsupported values retain `ubuntu-latest`; pushes
and forks remain hosted. Allowed `ttr-selfhosted-<host>` values are defined by `HOST_LABELS` in
`scripts/ci/self-hosted-policy.js`. Leave the variable unset until a runner is
registered and independently qualified. Clearing it restores hosted selection for new jobs.
This source change does not register runners or change fork approval settings.

The routing condition requires a PR with matching head/base repository IDs and
names. Jobs explicitly grant only `contents: read`, carry no secrets or tokened
Turbo inputs, disable persistent Bun caching and retain restore-only PR Turbo
caches. Push jobs carrying credentials remain hosted. The required Test root-script job runs
`scripts/ci/self-hosted-policy.js` across all workflows; regression tests include
missing guards, elevated permissions, secret references, cache writers, fork
fallback and invalid variable controls. Source tests establish policy behavior;
actual host qualification and execution require separate runtime evidence.

## Calendar owning-suite timings

The `calendar-native` job in `mail-calendar-tasks-builds.yaml` reports Calendar,
Web and shared Tasks UI tests as three sequential steps after supplier builds,
the native Calendar build and the tracked route-tree drift guard. Each suite
inherits the job's production profile and CI fixtures. Default success conditions
keep emitted-config qualification, binding and consumer type checks, artifact
sealing, runtime acceptance and restore qualification behind successful tests.

Step separation has zero expected green-path saving. Measure each suite on the
same exact-commit CI run before proposing parallelism, including supplier/build
and artifact-transfer costs. Preserve the generated route tree used by the accepted
build in any future handoff. OAuth tests skipped without integration credentials
provide no integration coverage. Regression coverage is in
`scripts/ci/calendar-suite-steps.test.mjs`, loaded by the artifact regressions.


## Disposable Redis for web unit shards

`scripts/ci/run-test-shard.js` owns one disposable Redis lifecycle when its
computed shard includes `@tuturuuu/web`. Both Test workflow shard jobs and the
public merged-main unit path call this runner; neither needs a separate service.
Non-web shards and paused runtimes do not provision a fixture.

Direct `bun run --cwd apps/web test` calls use `scripts/ci/run-web-tests.js`,
which applies the same fixture boundary before forwarding Vitest arguments.
This covers Web-owning tests in the Mail/Calendar/Tasks workflow without a
workflow service. An inherited explicitly opted-in endpoint is reused by local
and Turbo-filtered child environments; direct hosted calls provision their own
disposable fixture.

Automatic provisioning requires GitHub-hosted Linux. The helper pulls the official
`library/redis` image by immutable digest, publishes only an ephemeral loopback
port, disables persistence, and caps Redis memory at 16 MiB inside a 64 MiB
container. Readiness has 30 bounded attempts. Cleanup matches the random owner
name and label, removes only that container and its volumes, and fails the run
when cleanup fails. SIGINT/SIGTERM terminate the owned test process group before
cleanup. Forced host termination still relies on the ephemeral runner teardown.

Local execution requires an independently owned fixture and explicit
`LIVE_MINT_TEST_REDIS_DISPOSABLE=1`, plus exactly one
`LIVE_MINT_TEST_REDIS_PORT` (loopback) or absolute
`LIVE_MINT_TEST_REDIS_SOCKET`. Production Redis URLs and credentials never select
this endpoint. Local execution does not start Docker or pull an image. Turbo
hashes the disposable opt-in and passes the ephemeral endpoint to test tasks.
The real Redis suite retains its refusal without explicit opt-in.

Verify lifecycle controls with `node --test scripts/ci/disposable-redis.test.js
scripts/ci/test-shards.test.js`. On an admitted local fixture, run the real web
`src/lib/live/mint-cap.redis.test.ts` suite with one worker. Docker startup and
signal cleanup require an ephemeral Linux CI receipt before claiming live
container coverage; injected command tests cover local failure paths.

Image provenance: [official Redis image](https://hub.docker.com/_/redis) and
[Docker port publication](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/).
The helper pins the SHA-256 verified from the registry manifest index for
`7.4-alpine`; review and reverify the digest before updating it.

## Web Vercel route budget

The Web preview and production workflows count routing rules in
`.vercel/output/config.json` after the Vercel build. The maximum is 2,000,
leaving 48 rules below Vercel’s deployment limit. Web production is served from
Cloudflare; the Vercel build remains only as the legacy platform deploy and
marker, so do not grow toward the limit. The count appears in the
**Check Web route budget** step. Treat the **Route (app)** listing as a source
inventory because one Next.js endpoint can produce several routing rules.

Keep the URL and method contracts when consolidating workspace APIs. Selected
legacy resource groups share generated catch-all wrappers. Update the underlying
handlers and regenerate wrappers with
`node scripts/generate-web-api-route-wrappers.js --write`.

## Offline Vercel Release Recipe

The Calendar stage publisher reads a committed record from
`scripts/ci/release-vercel-config.mjs`. Tests pin its nine literal values,
workflow environment, input mappings, project secret name and CLI version.
Invalid records throw `VERCEL_CONFIG_INVALID` during module import, before a
stage stop receipt can be written. The stage publisher retains its 37 runtime
guard codes and permits only pull, build and skip-domain deploy commands.

The queue adapter and lifecycle modes are offline mechanisms with injected ports;
they provide no provider transport or active dispatch integration. Each job names
one phase. Authority approval, canonical target locks, current epoch, stop revision
and durable phase intent precede injected effects. An uncertain accepted effect
requires reconciliation; it must never be replayed automatically.

Calendar promote and rollback require the production-only environment and ref,
separate from staging, plus their respective approval references. Watch checks
smoke and error-rate evidence within duration, timeout and sample bounds. Fast
probes are spaced across the observation window. A threshold emits
`rollback-required`; restoring the recorded preimage requires a separately
authorized rollback phase and alias readback. Queue admission alone does not
authorize a release. Production activation and environment/path approvals remain
separate gates.

When an exact-source dispatch pins publisher files, preserve that pin set until
the dispatch is consumed or expires. A config-driven publisher also requires its
imported record in the reviewed blob set.

Lifecycle receipts preserve their fixed failure code and phase through the queue
boundary. Pre-effect policy failures are failed, cancellation fences are stopped,
and uncertain effects remain unknown. Success requires verified final authority
acknowledgements. Canonical locks cover the shared alias across environments;
Vercel alias writes are not atomic compare-and-swap operations, so exclusion
requires the authority lock.

Promotion consumes a succeeded stage receipt; watch and rollback consume a
succeeded promote receipt. The authority supplies the predecessor digest and
exact approval verification. Running source files and validated configuration
produce the recipe/config digests; caller-supplied digest agreement alone is
insufficient. Qualification evidence and the recorded rollback preimage remain
bound to that predecessor. Production ancestry is checked against the fetched
`origin/production` ref, and the runtime ref defaults to `GITHUB_REF`. Fetch that
ref in an approved workflow before activation. An already-applied alias is
verified without another write. Watch schedules fixed offsets and gives every
started probe its full timeout, allowing at most one probe timeout beyond the
observation window.
